title: Internal-module transport of the balanced K-flat scalar mate and its transpose
statement:
Let $a:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion of schemes [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change, def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $A_T=\Lambda_T$, $B_T=\Lambda'_T$ for $T=U,X$, with coefficient maps $a_T$ and canonical isomorphisms $\alpha_A:j^{-1}A_X\cong A_U$, $\alpha_B:j^{-1}B_X\cong B_U$ [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Work in ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $T_T=B_T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_T}-$ and $r_T=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_T})$, with the specified scalar adjunctions $T_T\dashv r_T$ and their units $\eta_T$. Let $R_A=D(j_A^*)$, $R_B=D(j_B^*)$ be the levelwise module-object pullbacks [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Define $d:R_Ar_X\xrightarrow{\sim}r_UR_B$ to be the degreewise localized action identification: after the balanced collapses $x\otimes n\mapsto\alpha^{-1}(x)n$, it is the identity on $j^{-1}N$, whose two $A_U$-actions agree by $\alpha_B^{-1}a_U=j^{-1}(a_X)\alpha_A^{-1}$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars].

For each coefficient ring $R_T=A_T,B_T$, use the canonical exact underlying-sheaf-preserving equivalence $E_{R_T}$ from internal modules to modules over its reconstructed section-ring sheaf [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. Use the canonical scalar-extension/restriction comparisons, including their units and counits, of that node, and the pullback comparisons for the section-ring isomorphisms induced by $\alpha$ [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. Transport the inverse balanced K-flat tensor/pullback comparison of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] through these fixed equivalences and comparisons; denote the resulting natural transformation by $\theta:T_UR_A\to R_BT_X$. Here the sectionwise comparison is taken for $h=j^{-1}$ with the section rings identified via $\alpha$, and its value on a flat-term K-flat representative is the inverse of the localized balanced comparison $\chi_j$ of that node.

Then $\theta$ is an isomorphism on the entire unbounded derived category, is precisely the scalar-adjunction mate of $d$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and for every $V\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_X})$ has the specified transpose
$$r_U(\theta_V)\circ\eta_{U,R_AV}=d_{T_XV}\circ R_A(\eta_{X,V}).$$
This uses the specified internal derived scalar units, rather than independently chosen adjunction structures. No flatness of $a$ or boundedness of $V$ is assumed.

proof.text: For $R=A,B$, collapse $j_R^*M=R_U\otimes_{j^{-1}R_X}j^{-1}M$ by $x\otimes m\mapsto\alpha_R^{-1}(x)m$. Its inverse is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$: balancing gives $x\otimes m=1\otimes\alpha_R^{-1}(x)m$. Thus this is the lift of geometric inverse image after the ring isomorphism $\alpha_R$. The latter is invertible by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]; the transported inverse image is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact]. Underlying-sheaf-preserving exact reconstruction [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] therefore identifies both internal pullbacks with these exact section-module pullbacks. In particular their ordinary unbounded derived functors are obtained termwise, as in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. No hypothesis on flatness of $a$ enters this argument.

proof.text: Use a bar for the section-module derived functors and $E_{R_T}$ also for the exact derived equivalences. Set $u_T:E_{A_T}r_T\cong\bar r_TE_{B_T}$ and $c_T:E_{B_T}T_T\cong\bar T_TE_{A_T}$. By [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] these are the specified scalar comparisons, and $c_T$ identifies the entire adjunction with the barred one, including units and counits. Set $p:E_{A_U}R_A\cong\bar R_AE_{A_X}$ and $q:E_{B_U}R_B\cong\bar R_BE_{B_X}$, using the canonical pullback comparisons of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], localized termwise. Exactness from step 1 ensures that this localization needs no resolution. Consequently $c_T$ is exactly the normalized left-adjoint comparison associated with $u_T$ in part (1) of [lem-sfb-equivalence-square-inverse-mate-coherence]; uniqueness there excludes a different choice of scalar-adjunction normalization.

proof.text:
Let $\bar d:\bar R_A\bar r_X\cong\bar r_U\bar R_B$ be the section action identification, using the section-ring isomorphisms induced by $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$. The right-square compatibility required by part (3) of the equivalence-square lemma is
$$(\bar d E_{B_X})\circ(\bar R_Au_X)\circ(pr_X)=(\bar r_Uq)\circ(u_UR_B)\circ E_{A_U}(d).$$
Check this before localization. After the balanced collapses of step 1, each route is the identity on $j^{-1}N$: reconstruction preserves the underlying sheaf and restriction is the identity on it. Its $A_U$-action on either route sends $(x,n)$ to $(j^{-1}a_X)(\alpha_A^{-1}(x))n=\alpha_B^{-1}(a_U(x))n$. The equality is exactly the coefficient square of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. This checks linearity as well as equality of the maps. Naturality follows because these identity maps commute with every module morphism. Apply the equality in each degree of a complex and localize; the fixed restriction and pullback comparisons are those localizations by step 2, so the displayed derived square follows.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] to $h=j^{-1}$ on the small pro-étale sites, identifying the pulled-back section rings via $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$. Its $A_X=h^{-1}A_Y,B_X=h^{-1}B_Y$ convention corresponds here to the sites $U,X$, respectively; the commuting coefficient square checked in step 3 supplies the ring-map compatibility. It gives a natural isomorphism $\bar\theta:\bar T_U\bar R_A\to\bar R_B\bar T_X$, the inverse scalar-adjunction mate of $\bar d$. On flat-term K-flat representatives it is precisely the inverse of the localized balanced comparison. The conclusion of that node already holds on the entire ordinary unbounded derived category, without flatness of the coefficient map. Thus no inference from degreewise cohomology or from bounded representatives is needed here.

proof.text:
Let $\beta:T_UR_A\to R_BT_X$ be the inverse mate of $d$ for the specified internal scalar adjunctions. Apply part (3) of [lem-sfb-equivalence-square-inverse-mate-coherence] with $(J,U)=(T_X,r_X)$, $(J',U')=(T_U,r_U)$, $(P,Q)=(R_A,R_B)$ and four equivalences $(E_{A_X},E_{B_X},E_{A_U},E_{B_U})$. Its $u,u',j,j',p,q$ are $u_X,u_U,c_X,c_U,p,q$ from step 2. Step 3 proves its right-square hypothesis. Its conclusion is the actual equality
$$(\bar R_Bc_X)\circ(qT_X)\circ E_{B_U}(\beta)=(\bar\theta E_{A_X})\circ(\bar T_Up)\circ(c_UR_A).$$
Solving this equality for $E_{B_U}(\beta)$ gives exactly the transport defining $\theta$ in the statement, since step 4 identifies $\bar\theta$ with the prescribed inverse balanced comparison. The equivalence is faithful, so $\beta=\theta$. Every comparison in this equation and $\bar\theta$ is invertible; equivalently the invertibility conclusion of the same lemma gives that $\theta$ is invertible. This proves both the global isomorphism and the specified mate assertion, retaining all comparison maps.

proof.text:
Write $\varepsilon_U$ for the counit of the specified internal scalar adjunction. The inverse-mate formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], now for $\theta=\beta$, is
$$\theta_V=\varepsilon_{U,R_BT_XV}\circ T_U(d_{T_XV})\circ T_UR_A(\eta_{X,V}).$$
Put $k=d_{T_XV}\circ R_A(\eta_{X,V}):R_AV\to r_UR_BT_XV$. Naturality of the actual unit $\eta_U$ gives
$$r_U(\theta_V)\circ\eta_{U,R_AV}=r_U(\varepsilon_{U,R_BT_XV})\circ r_UT_U(k)\circ\eta_{U,R_AV}=r_U(\varepsilon_{U,R_BT_XV})\circ\eta_{U,r_UR_BT_XV}\circ k=k,$$
where the last equality is the right-adjoint triangle identity for $T_U\dashv r_U$. This is the required transpose. The units and counit here are precisely those fixed in step 2, so the calculation does not replace the published adjunction by an independently chosen structure.
